newsitem.title: USA: AT&T plans new U.S.-Europe undersea cable system.
newsitem.headline: AT&T plans new U.S.-Europe undersea cable system.

text.p: AT&T Corp. said Monday it signed a memorandum of understanding to build an undersea fiber optic cable network that will link the United States with southern Europe by July 1999.
The network, Columbus III, is expected to span nearly 11,000 kilometres (7,040 miles) and cost between $270 million and $310 million when completed.
It will be built with Telecom Italia, Telefonica de Espana, S.A. and Companhia Portuguesa Radio Marconi, S.A. The companies will own and operate cable stations in their respective home countries.
The system will transmit voice, data and images with an initial capacity of up to 10 gigabits per second (gbps). It can be upgraded to transmit up to 40 gbps, or nearly 490,000 simultaneous calls.
The agreement calls for the cable to form a collapsed ring connecting Florida and St. Croix, U.S. Virgin Islands, to Lisbon and the Azores in Portugal, Conil in Spain, and Mazara, Italy.

The new system is important because the explosive demand for high-speed telecommunications in the region has nearly exhausted capacity on the U.S.-Europe segment of the Columbus II undersea cable network, AT&T said. That 12,000-kilometre (7,680 mile) cable links Spain, Portugal and Italy with West Palm Beach, Fla., St. Thomas in the U.S. Virgin Islands and Cancun, Mexico.

AT&T said Friday that it would sell its underwater telecommunications cable business to industrial conglomerate Tyco International Ltd. for about $850 million. The AT&T Submarine Systems Inc. business makes electronic components that join the cable and also installs, supplies and maintains the systems.
